l: Surah 75: The Resurrection (Al-Qiyaama), Surah 75: The Resurrection (Al-Qiyaama)
s: Surah 75: The Resurrection (Al-Qiyaama) describes the Day of Resurrection, the fate of man, death, and the resurrection of the dead. It also instructs that the reading and explanation of the Scripture rest upon Allah.
Allah is described as able to restore man's bones and very fingers and to bring the dead to life. Allah shapes and fashions man from a drop of fluid and makes of him a pair, male and female.

l: Day of Resurrection, Surah 75: The Resurrection (Al-Qiyaama)
s: The Day of Resurrection is a day when sight is confounded, the moon is eclipsed, and the sun and moon are united. Man will be told what he sent before and left behind, and will have recourse to his Lord.

Man questions whether his bones will be assembled, wants to deny what is before him, and asks when the Day of Resurrection will be. He is a witness against himself despite his excuses, loves the fleeting Now, neglects the Hereafter, and will face judgment according to his trust, prayer, denial, and conduct.
Man loves the fleeting Now and neglects the Hereafter.
The Hereafter is neglected by man, who instead loves the fleeting Now. On the Day of Resurrection, faces will be resplendent looking toward their Lord, while other faces will be despondent.
As life comes up to the throat, men ask where the wizard is who can save the dying person. The person knows that it is the parting, agony is heaped on agony, and he is driven unto his Lord.

l: resurrection of the dead, Surah 75: The Resurrection (Al-Qiyaama)
s: The resurrection of the dead is affirmed by Allah's ability to restore man's bones and even his fingers. Allah is able to bring the dead to life after creating man from a drop of fluid, shaping him, and making him male and female.

Surah 77: The Emissaries (Al-Mursalaat), revealed at Mecca, concerns the promised event and the Day of Decision. It describes emissary winds and other forces that revive vegetation, winnow, bring down the Reminder, and excuse or warn. The unit warns the repudiators and guilty of punishment, including the flame and doom they denied. It describes the reward of those who kept their duty in shade, fountains, and desired fruits.

l: Surah 77: The Emissaries (Al-Mursalaat), Surah 77: The Emissaries (Al-Mursalaat)
s: It is revealed at Mecca and concerns the promised event, the Day of Decision, the repudiators, the guilty, and those who kept their duty.
They are sent one after another and are associated with raging hurricanes, the revival of earth's vegetation, winnowing, and bringing down the Reminder to excuse or warn.

l: the promised event, Surah 77: The Emissaries (Al-Mursalaat)
s: It will befall, and its coming is associated with the stars being put out, the sky being riven asunder, the mountains being blown away, and the messengers being brought to their appointed time.

l: the Day of Decision, Surah 77: The Emissaries (Al-Mursalaat)
s: It is the appointed day when the former and latter folk are brought together and judgment is made clear. On that day, the repudiators are warned of woe, while those who kept their duty receive reward.
They are threatened with destruction and woe, and are told to eat and take their ease only a little because they are guilty.
They repeatedly face woe on the Day of Decision. They deny the doom, do not speak or offer excuses, and do not bow down when told to bow.
They are created from a base fluid laid up in a safe abode for a known term. They are brought together with the men of old on the Day of Decision.
It is made a receptacle for both the living and the dead. It contains high mountains and provides sweet water.
It is the punishment that the repudiators used to deny, and they are told to depart toward it.
It has a threefold shadow that offers no relief or shelter. It throws up sparks like castles or like camels of bright yellow hue.

l: those who kept their duty, Surah 77: The Emissaries (Al-Mursalaat)
s: They are amid shade and fountains with fruits such as they desire. They are told to eat, drink, and welcome their reward for what they did.

Surah 80: He frowned (Abasa) concerns a man who turns away from a blind man while attending to one who thinks himself independent. It teaches that the Admonishment is available for whoever will heed it and describes man's creation, death, burial, and return to life. It recounts how food and provision come through rain, crops, fruits, and grasses for people and cattle. It describes the Shout and the day when people flee from their closest relatives, with bright faces for some and dust-covered, darkened faces for disbelievers and the wicked.

l: Surah 80: He frowned (Abasa), Surah 80: He frowned (Abasa)
s: It describes one who frowned and turned away because the blind man came unto him. It teaches that the Admonishment is on honoured, exalted, purified leaves set down by noble and righteous scribes, and ends by describing the contrasting faces of people on the day of the Shout.
He came unto the man with earnest purpose and fear, but the man was distracted from him.

He is described as self-destroyed and ungrateful, created from a drop of seed, proportioned, given an easy way, caused to die and be buried, and brought again to life when commanded. He has not done what was commanded of him, and on the day of the Shout he flees from his brother, mother, father, wife, and children because he has enough concern to make him heedless of others.
It is an Admonishment that whoever wills may heed. It is on honoured leaves that are exalted and purified, set down by noble and righteous scribes.
It is described as the time when a man is brought again to life after he has died and been buried.

Man is told to consider his food and how water is poured in showers, the earth is split in clefts, and grain, grapes, green fodder, olive-trees, palm-trees, garden-closes, fruits, and grasses are brought forth.
It consists of the grain, grapes, green fodder, olive-trees, palm-trees, garden-closes, fruits, and grasses provided for people and their cattle.
It comes suddenly on the day when a man flees from his brother and from his mother, father, wife, and children.

l: the day of the Shout, Surah 80: He frowned (Abasa)
s: On it, every man has concern enough to make him heedless of others. Faces are bright, laughing, and rejoicing at good news for some, while other faces have dust upon them and are veiled in darkness.
They are among those whose faces on that day have dust upon them and are veiled in darkness.
They are among those whose faces on that day have dust upon them and are veiled in darkness.

Surah 81: The Overthrowing (At-Takwir) describes signs of the Last Day and what every soul will know about its deeds. It concerns the sun, stars, hills, animals, seas, souls, the girl-child that was buried alive, the sky, hell, and the Garden. It affirms that the revelation is the word of an honoured messenger, supported by the Lord of the Throne, and that your comrade is not mad. It calls creation to remember and walk straight, while stating that none wills unless Allah willeth.

l: Surah 81: The Overthrowing (At-Takwir), Surah 81: The Overthrowing (At-Takwir)
s: Surah 81: The Overthrowing (At-Takwir) describes the overthrowing of the sun, the falling of the stars, the moving of the hills, and other events of the Last Day. It states that every soul will know what it has made ready and calls creation to walk straight.
Souls are reunited, and every soul will know what it has made ready.

l: girl-child that was buried alive, Surah 81: The Overthrowing (At-Takwir)
s: The girl-child that was buried alive is asked for what sin she was slain.
Hell is lighted.
The Garden is brought nigh.
The honoured messenger is described as mighty, established in the presence of the Lord of the Throne, obeyed, and trustworthy.

l: Lord of the Throne, Surah 81: The Overthrowing (At-Takwir)
s: The Lord of the Throne is the presence in which the honoured messenger is established.
Your comrade is not mad, has beheld Him on the clear horizon, and is not avid of the Unseen.
Creation is addressed as the recipient of the reminder. Whoever among creation wills may walk straight.
Allah is identified as the one whose will determines that none will walk straight unless He willeth, and He is called the Lord of Creation.

The unit describes the signs accompanying the Cleaving, including the heaven being cleft, the planets dispersed, the seas poured forth, and the sepulchres overturned. It states that each soul will know what it sent before and left behind. Man is questioned about his carelessness toward his Lord, who created and fashioned him, while guardians record all deeds. The righteous will be in delight, the wicked in hell, and Allah's command will prevail on the Day of Judgment.
Allah is the Lord of man, and the absolute command on the Day of Judgment is His.
The heaven is cleft asunder.
The planets are dispersed.
The seas are poured forth.
The sepulchres are overturned.
A soul will know what it sent before and what it left behind. No soul will have power over any other soul on that day.
Man is questioned about what made him careless concerning his Lord. He was created, fashioned, proportioned, and cast into whatever form He willed.
The Judgment is denied by some. On its day, each soul will face the consequences of what it sent before and left behind.
Guardians are above man, generous and recording, and they know all that people do.
The righteous will be in delight.
The wicked will be in hell and will burn there on the Day of Judgment. They will not be absent from it.
Hell is where the wicked will be, burning on the Day of Judgment, and they will not be absent from it.

The unit condemns the defrauders, who demand full measure for themselves but cause others loss. It warns that mankind will be raised on the Awful Day to stand before Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, and that the repudiators of the Day of Judgment will face punishment in hell. It contrasts the guilty, who mock those who believed, with the righteous, who enjoy delight and drink from Tasnim. On that day, those who believed will have the laugh of disbelievers.

They demand full measure when taking from mankind, but when measuring or weighing for others, they cause them loss. They are warned of an Awful Day when they will be raised and stand before the Lord of the Worlds.
They will be raised again on the Awful Day and stand before the Lord of the Worlds.
It is the day when mankind will be raised and stand before the Lord of the Worlds.

l: Allah (Lord of the Worlds), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: Mankind will stand before Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, on the Awful Day. The righteous are brought near unto their Lord.
The text warns that the defrauders will be raised again and stand before the Lord of the Worlds.
They deny the Day of Judgment and are called criminal transgressors. Their record is in Sijjin, they will be covered from the mercy of their Lord, and they will burn in hell.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: The repudiators deny it, and none denies it save each criminal transgressor.
The repudiators will burn in hell, where they will be told that it is what they used to deny.
Their record is in Illiyin, a written record attested by those brought near unto their Lord. They are in delight, reclining on couches and receiving pure wine mixed with water from Tasnim.
The righteous are in delight, whose radiance is visible in their faces. They receive a pure, sealed wine and drink from Tasnim.
They used to laugh at those who believed, wink at one another when passing them, return to their own folk jesting, and say that those who believed had gone astray.
They were mocked by the guilty, but on the appointed day they will have the laugh of disbelievers while reclining on high couches and gazing.
The guilty used to laugh at those who believed, but on that day those who believed will have the laugh of disbelievers.

Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj) concerns the owners of the ditch who persecuted believers by witnessing them in a fuel-fed fire. It condemns those who persecute believing men and women without repentance and promises them hell, while promising believers who do good works Gardens beneath which rivers flow. It describes Allah as the Sovereign, Witness, Forgiving, Loving, and Doer of what He wills, and mentions the hosts of Pharaoh and Thamud. It declares that the Qur'an is glorious and kept on a guarded tablet.

l: Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: It recounts the destruction of the owners of the ditch and their persecution of believers. It also describes the fate of persecutors and the reward of believers who do good works.

Allah is described as the Mighty, the Owner of Praise, the Sovereign of the heavens and the earth, and the Witness of all things. He is also described as Forgiving, Loving, Lord of the Throne of Glory, and Doer of what He wills.

l: owners of the ditch, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: The owners of the ditch sat by a fuel-fed fire and witnessed what they did to the believers. They were self-destroyed because they persecuted believers who had naught against them except that they believed in Allah.
The fire was fuel-fed, and the owners of the ditch sat by it while witnessing what they did to the believers.
The believers were persecuted by the owners of the ditch because they believed in Allah. Those who believe and do good works are promised Gardens beneath which rivers flow.

l: persecutors of believers, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: Persecutors of believing men and believing women are warned that, if they do not repent, they will face the doom of hell and the doom of burning.
Hell is the promised fate of those who persecute believing men and believing women and do not repent.
Gardens beneath which rivers flow are promised to those who believe and do good works. They are described as the Great Success.

l: punishment of Allah, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: The punishment of Allah is described as stern.
The Qur'an is described as glorious and as being on a guarded tablet.

Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq) concerns the Morning Star, human creation, resurrection, and the Qur'an. It says that every human soul has a guardian and that hidden thoughts will be searched out. It declares the Qur'an to be a conclusive word and describes a plot against Muhammad. The disbelievers are to be given a respite and dealt with gently for a while.

l: Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq), Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq)
s: It concerns the Morning Star, human creation, resurrection, the Qur'an, Muhammad, and the disbelievers. It declares that the Qur'an is a conclusive word and describes a plot against Muhammad.

l: Morning Star, Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq)
s: It is described as a piercing Star. The text asks what will tell about the Morning Star and swears by it.
It is described as a conclusive word and not a pleasantry.
A plot is made against him by the disbelievers, and he is told to give them a respite and deal gently with them for a while.
They plot a plot against Muhammad. They are to be given a respite and dealt with gently for a while.

Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa) concerns praise of the Lord the Most High, who creates, measures, guides, brings forth pasturage, and turns it to stubble. It states that Allah knows what is disclosed and hidden, and that the way to ease will be made accessible. The passage urges reminding people, describing the heedful as successful and the hapless as flung into the great Fire. It teaches that the Hereafter is better and more lasting than the life of the world and says this is found in the former scrolls, the Books of Abraham and Moses.

l: Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: It praises the Lord the Most High and urges remembrance, prayer, and reminding. It teaches that the successful person grows, remembers the name of the Lord, and prays, while the hapless flouts the reminder and is flung to the great Fire.

l: Allah (Lord the Most High), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: Allah is described as the Lord the Most High, who creates, disposes, measures, guides, brings forth pasturage, and turns it to russet stubble. Allah knows what is disclosed and what remains hidden, and wills what is excepted from being forgotten.

l: the great Fire, Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: The great Fire is the place to which the most hapless person will be flung. In it, he will neither die nor live.

l: the life of the world, Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: The life of the world is preferred by some over the Hereafter. It is described as inferior to and less lasting than the Hereafter.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: The Hereafter is described as better and more lasting than the life of the world.

l: the Books of Abraham and Moses, Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: The Books of Abraham and Moses are identified as the former scrolls in which this teaching is found.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: prince is forbidden Paradise (if he oppresses the subject and dies)
q: There is no prince who oppresseth the subject and dieth, but God forbiddeth Paradise to him.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: slave is obeyed obedience (when appointed to rule, even if his head is like a dried grape)
q: If a negro slave is appointed to rule over you, hear him, and obey him, though his head should be like a dried grape.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: obedience is due to lawful commands
q: There is no obedience due to sinful commands, nor to any other than what is lawful.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: obedience is not due to sinful commands
q: There is no obedience due to sinful commands, nor to any other than what is lawful.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: Prophet of God orders obedience their orders (it is on them to be just and good)
q: He said, “Ye must hear them and obey their orders: it is on them to be just and good, and on you to be obedient and submissive.”

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: Government is inquired about on Day of Resurrection (unless its holder is worthy, just, and good)
q: Government is a trust from God, and verily government will be at the Day of Resurrection a cause of inquiry, unless he who hath taken it be worthy of it and have acted justly and done good.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: anger is withheld by strong (the strong withhold themselves from it)
q: He is not strong or powerful who throws people down, but he is strong who withholds himself from anger.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: anger is managed by sitting (when one becomes angry)
q: When one of you getteth angry, he must sit down, and if his anger goeth away from sitting, so much the better;

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: anger is managed by lying down (if it does not go away from sitting)
q: if not, let him lie down.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: king is a God’s shadow upon the earth
q: Verily a king is God’s shadow upon the earth;

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: subject turns to king (when oppressed)
q: and every one oppressed turneth to him:

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: king receives rewards (when he does justice)
q: then when the king doeth justice, for him are rewards and gratitude from his subject:

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: king receives gratitude (from his subject when he does justice)
q: then when the king doeth justice, for him are rewards and gratitude from his subject:

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: king bears sin (when he oppresses)
q: but, if the king oppresseth, on him is his sin, and for the oppressed resignation.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: subject shows resignation (when oppressed by the king)
q: but, if the king oppresseth, on him is his sin, and for the oppressed resignation.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: medicine is a means of curing pain (created by God for every pain except age)
q: O servants of God use medicine: because God hath not created a pain without a remedy for it, to be the means of curing it, except age;

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: God creates medicine (as a means of curing pain)
q: O servants of God use medicine: because God hath not created a pain without a remedy for it, to be the means of curing it, except age;

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: pain has remedy (except when it is age)
q: because God hath not created a pain without a remedy for it, to be the means of curing it, except age;

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: God is not loving to person (when the person is not loving to God’s creatures and his own children)
q: He who is not loving to God’s creatures and to his own children, God will not be loving to him.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: vanity excludes God (everything is vanity except God)
q: The truest words spoken by any poet are those of Lebīd, who said, “Know that everything is vanity except God.”

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: meekness is a branch of faith
q: Meekness and shame are two branches of faith,

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: shame is a branch of faith
q: Meekness and shame are two branches of faith,

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: knowledge has calamity forgetfulness
q: The calamity of knowledge is forgetfulness,

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: knowledge is lost by speaking of it to the unworthy
q: and to lose knowledge is this, to speak of it to the unworthy.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: road of knowledge leads to Paradise (when pursued)
q: Whoso pursueth the road of knowledge, God will direct him to the road of Paradise;

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: God directs road of knowledge (toward the road of Paradise when it is pursued)
q: Whoso pursueth the road of knowledge, God will direct him to the road of Paradise;

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: Moses is acquainted by God (with his tribe’s worshipping a calf)
q: verily God acquainted Moses of his tribe’s worshipping a calf,

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: tables are broken by Moses (after he saw the calf his tribe had made)
q: but when Moses went to his tribe, and saw with his eyes the calf they had made, he threw down the tables and broke them.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: painter is in Hell Fire
q: Every painter is in Hell Fire;

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: Jesus is called God (by Christians)
q: as the Christians are in praising Jesus, Mary’s Son, by calling him God, and the Son of God;

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: God has pleasure in father’s pleasure
q: God’s pleasure is in a father’s pleasure,

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: God appoints person (at the Day of Resurrection for every picture drawn)
q: and God will appoint a person at the Day of Resurrection for every picture he shall have drawn, to punish him, and they will punish him in Hell.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: God has displeasure in father’s displeasure
q: and God’s displeasure is a father’s displeasure.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: friends are best near God (when they are the best among friends)
q: The best person near God is the best amongst his friends;

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: neighbours are best near God (when they are the best person in their neighbourhood)
q: and the best of neighbours near God is the best person in his own neighbourhood.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: deliberation is pleasing to God (in undertaking)
q: Deliberation in undertaking is pleasing to God,

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: Day of Resurrection is a time of punishment (for those who draw pictures)
q: and God will appoint a person at the Day of Resurrection for every picture he shall have drawn, to punish him, and they will punish him in Hell.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: Death is a dreadful event
q: Verily death is dreadful: therefore when ye see a bier stand up.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: soul is brought to celestial regions (when it belongs to a faithful believer)
q: Then the soul cometh out like the smell of the best musk, so that verily it is handed from one angel to another, till they bring it to the doors of the celestial regions.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: faithful are happy at soul (when a faithful soul arrives)
q: Then they bring it to the souls of the faithful, and they are very happy at its coming; more than ye are at the coming of one of your family after a long journey.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: soul has scent worst stench of a dead body (when leaving an infidel)
q: Then it cometh out with a disagreeable smell, worse than the worst stench of a dead body, until they bring it upon the earth, and they say, “What an extraordinary bad smell this is;” till they bring it to the souls of the infidels.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: Prophet of God respects bier (regardless of the deceased person's religion)
q: A bier was passing, and the Prophet stood up for it; and we stood with him and said, “O Prophet! verily this bier is of a Jewish woman; we must not respect it.” Then the Prophet said, “Verily death is dreadful: therefore when ye see a bier stand up.”

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: people of the graves receive greeting from Prophet of God (with a prayer for forgiveness)
q: The Prophet passed by graves in Medina, and turned his face towards them, and said, “Peace be to you, O people of the graves. God forgive us and you! Ye have passed on before us, and we are following you.”

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: Mālik keeps Hell Fire (as keeper of hell)
q: and the person who was lighting the fire was Mālik, the keeper of hell;

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 2)
s: Gabriel conducts Prophet of God (in the vision)
q: and we who conducted you are one of us Gabriel, and the other Michael;
